mainTopic: The story of רבי עקיבא and his wife: poverty, twenty-four years of learning, the release of her father's נדר, and the six sources of his wealth.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a poor sage, רבי יהודה, who shows a messenger hidden wealth but says he does not want to enjoy this world. The גמרא then tells the famous story of רבי עקיבא and his wife, the daughter of the rich man כלבא שבוע. Her father cuts her off with a נדר of הנאה, but she marries רבי עקיבא anyway, and they live in deep poverty, sleeping on straw. She sends him to learn תורה for twelve years. When he comes home, he overhears her say she would gladly have him learn twelve more, so he goes back. He returns with 24,000 pairs of students and tells them that all his תורה and theirs belongs to her. Her father then has his נדר released. The amud ends by listing how רבי עקיבא became rich from six things: his father-in-law, a ship's ram figure, a log full of coins, the סרוקיתא, and a noble lady. The details of the last items continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The sage shows hidden wealth but refuses to enjoy this world
steps.stepSummary: The earlier story ends. The sage lifts his mat to show the messenger what is underneath, then explains that he chooses not to benefit from this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He lifted the mat and said to the messenger: 'See what is here.' But, he said, 'I do not want to enjoy benefit in this world.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story from before. The poor sage shows that he could have wealth if he wanted it, and explains why he stays poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now he looked poor. Lifting the mat shows his poverty is a choice, not a lack. His closing line gives the reason: he does not want his reward in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: a mat (a woven mat he was sitting on)
it is not pleasing to me / I do not want

steps.whatToRemember: The sage's poverty was his own choice. He gave up enjoying this world on purpose.

phrases.english: He lifted the mat
and said to the messenger:
See what there is here.
phrases.notes: He's showing the messenger that he could have money if he wanted it.

phrases.english: However, it is not pleasing to me
to have benefit in this world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sage could have been rich, but he chose not to take benefit in this world.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's engagement and the father's vow
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא becomes engaged to the daughter of כלבא שבוע. Her father makes a נדר forbidding her any benefit from his property, but she marries רבי עקיבא anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא became engaged to the daughter of כלבא שבוע. When כלבא שבוע heard, he made a vow forbidding her from benefiting from any of his property. She went and married him anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story, connected to the last one because it is also about a poor תלמיד חכם. It sets up the background: a rich father cuts off his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father uses a נדר of הנאה, so his daughter may not benefit from anything he owns. This is the reason the couple ends up so poor. Her choice to marry anyway shows her loyalty to רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of a very rich man in ירושלים
he made her vow / forbade her by vow from benefit

steps.whyThisMatters: This story fits מסכת נדרים because the whole poverty of the couple comes from a נדר of הנאה.

phrases.english: To Rabbi Akiva there became betrothed
the daughter of (bar) Kalba Savua.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word 'בר' in the round brackets and some don't. Either way it's the same rich man.

phrases.english: (Bar) Kalba Savua heard,
he made a vow forbidding her benefit from all his property.
She went and married him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story on the same theme of a poor תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father cut his daughter off with a נדר, and she married רבי עקיבא anyway.

steps.title: Sleeping on straw and the promise of a golden crown
steps.stepSummary: The couple sleeps in a straw barn in winter. רבי עקיבא picks straw from his wife's hair and tells her that if he could, he would give her a ירושלים דדהבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In winter they slept in a straw barn, and he would pick the straw out of her hair. He said to her: 'If I had the means, I would put a Jerusalem of Gold on you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes how poor the couple was. It also shows how much רבי עקיבא wished he could honor his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They cannot afford a real bed, so they sleep on straw. His promise of a golden crown shows his love and his wish to reward her. It also hints at what will come later in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: a straw barn / storehouse of straw
a 'Jerusalem of Gold', a golden crown

phrases.english: In the winter they would sleep in a straw barn,
he would pick out for her
the straw from her hair.
He said to her: If I had the means,
I would put on you a Jerusalem of Gold.
phrases.notes: This is a piece of golden jewelry for the head, a kind of crown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of the father's נדר: the couple lives in poverty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They were very poor, and רבי עקיבא longed to honor his wife.

steps.title: אליהו comes asking for straw
steps.stepSummary: אליהו comes disguised as a poor man and asks for straw for his wife, who has just given birth. רבי עקיבא tells his wife to see that this man doesn't even have straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו came looking like an ordinary man and called at the door. He said: 'Give me a little straw. My wife has given birth and I have nothing to lay her on.' רבי עקיבא said to his wife: 'Look at this man, who doesn't even have straw.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how אליהו came to the couple dressed as a poor man. רבי עקיבא uses the visit to comfort his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The visitor is poorer than they are, because he has no straw at all. That lets רבי עקיבא show his wife that they still have something to be grateful for.

keyTerms.meaning: he appeared as / took the form of

phrases.english: Elijah came and appeared to them as a person
and was calling at the door.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַבוּ לִי פּוּרְתָּא דְתִיבְנָא
phrases.english: He said to them: Give me a bit of straw,
because my wife has given birth,
and I have nothing to lay her on.
Rabbi Akiva said to his wife:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזִי גַּבְרָא דַּאֲפִילּוּ תִּיבְנָא לָא אִית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: See a man who doesn't even have straw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the poverty scene with a visitor who is even poorer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing someone with even less lets רבי עקיבא comfort his wife.

steps.title: His wife sends him to learn תורה
steps.stepSummary: His wife tells רבי עקיבא to go learn. He studies for twelve years under רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: 'Go and be a student in the study hall.' He went and learned for twelve years before רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The story turns. רבי עקיבא's wife pushes him to leave home and learn תורה, and he goes for twelve years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even while they are poor, she cares more about his learning than about having him home. His greatness in תורה starts with her push.

keyTerms.meaning: the study hall (literally, the house of the teacher)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: זִיל הֱוֵי בֵּי רַב.
phrases.english: She said to him: Go, be a student in the study hall.
He went for twelve years
before Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: זִיל הֱוֵי בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The scene of poverty leads to the wife's decision to send him to learn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of his wife's push, רבי עקיבא learned תורה for twelve years.

steps.title: Coming home and overhearing an insult
steps.stepSummary: After twelve years, רבי עקיבא comes home. Behind the house he hears a wicked man telling his wife that her father was right to cut her off, because her husband doesn't suit her and has left her like a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the end of twelve years he was coming home. From behind his house he heard a wicked man saying to his wife: 'Your father treated you right. First, your husband is not your equal. And also, he has left you like a widow while he is alive all these years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי עקיבא back home. Before he goes in, he overhears someone mocking his wife. This sets up her answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wicked man gives two reasons the father was right: the husband is not a fitting match, and he left her alone for years. These words test the wife's commitment to his learning.

keyTerms.meaning: living widowhood (being like a widow while the husband is alive)

phrases.english: At the end of twelve years
he was coming to his house,
he heard from behind his house
a certain wicked man saying to his wife:
Your father did well by you,
first, because he is not like you.
phrases.notes: He means your husband isn't a fitting match for you.

phrases.english: And also: [he left you] in living widowhood
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: all these years.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִישְׁלַם תַּרְתֵּי סְרֵי שְׁנִין קָא אֲתָא לְבֵיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up when the twelve years of learning are over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wicked man mocks the wife for marrying רבי עקיבא and being left alone.

steps.title: Her answer and his return for twelve more years
steps.stepSummary: The wife answers that if her husband listened to her, he would stay away and learn another twelve years. רבי עקיבא takes this as permission and goes back for twelve more years.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: 'If he would listen to me, he would stay there another twelve years.' רבי עקיבא said: 'Since she has given me permission, I will go back.' He turned around, went, and stayed another twelve years.
steps.whatsHappening: The wife answers the wicked man by showing full support for her husband's learning. רבי עקיבא hears it and goes straight back to learn without even coming inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of complaining, she wants twelve more years of learning. רבי עקיבא treats her words as permission, so he returns at once and learns a total of twenty-four years.
steps.whatToRemember: His wife's support was the reason רבי עקיבא learned for twenty-four years. She gave up having him home so he could grow in תורה.
steps.confusionAlert: She is speaking to the wicked man, not to רבי עקיבא. He only overhears her, and that is why he says she 'gave permission'.

phrases.english: She said to him: If he would listen to me,
he would stay another twelve years.
He said: Since she has given me permission,
I will go back.
He turned around and went,
and was there another twelve years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wicked man's insult from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife wants him to learn twelve more years, and רבי עקיבא goes back to learn them.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא returns with 24,000 pairs of students
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא comes home with a huge following of students. Everyone goes out to greet him, and his wife goes out too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came back with twenty-four thousand pairs of students. Everyone went out to greet him, and she also got up to go out and greet him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story jumps ahead to the end of the second twelve years. רבי עקיבא comes home as a great teacher, and his wife goes out to meet him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in Step 6 the wicked man said she was left like a widow. Now the result of her sacrifice is clear: her husband returns as a famous רב with thousands of תלמידים. This sets up the moment where she has to face the crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: to greet him (literally, toward his face)

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא בְּעֶשְׂרִין וְאַרְבְּעָה אַלְפִין זוּגֵי תַלְמִידֵי.
phrases.english: He came with twenty-four thousand pairs of students.
Everyone went out to greet him,
and she too got up to go out to greet him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא בְּעֶשְׂרִין וְאַרְבְּעָה אַלְפִין זוּגֵי תַלְמִידֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבי עקיבא's second twelve years of learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא returns in great honor with 24,000 pairs of students, and his wife goes out to greet him.

steps.title: The wicked man mocks her, and she answers with a verse
steps.stepSummary: The wicked man asks where she thinks she is going. She answers with a פסוק: a righteous man knows the soul of his animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: That wicked man said to her: And where are you going? She said to him: "A righteous man knows the soul of his animal."
steps.whatsHappening: The same wicked man from Step 6 mocks her for thinking she belongs with this great רב. She answers with a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question suggests that a poor, shabby woman has no place near such an important man. She humbly compares herself to an animal that works for its owner. A צדיק understands what his loyal helper has gone through, so her husband will recognize her.

keyTerms.meaning: a righteous man knows the soul of his animal (משלי 12:10)

phrases.english: That wicked man said to her:
phrases.notes: This is the same man who mocked her back in Step 6.

phrases.english: And you, where are you going?
She said to him: "A righteous man knows the soul of his animal."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ הַהוּא רַשִּׁיעָא וְאַתְּ לְהֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: As she goes out to greet him, the wicked man from Step 6 challenges her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She trusts that her righteous husband will recognize what she gave up for him.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says all his תורה and theirs belongs to her
steps.stepSummary: The students push her away, but רבי עקיבא tells them to leave her alone, because his תורה and theirs is hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: She came to show herself to him, and the רבנן were pushing her away. He said to them: Leave her alone. What is mine and what is yours is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: She comes close to רבי עקיבא, and his students try to keep her back. He stops them and gives her full credit for all their learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves her פסוק right: the צדיק does know what she went through. Because she sent him to learn, all the תורה he gained belongs to her. All the תורה his students learned from him belongs to her too.

keyTerms.meaning: to show herself, to appear before

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the most famous lines in the גמרא. It shows that the one who makes תורה learning possible shares fully in it.

phrases.english: She came to show herself to him,
and the Rabbis were pushing her away.
phrases.notes: Here רבנן means the students around רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: He said to them: Leave her alone,
what is mine and what is yours is hers.
phrases.notes: He means the תורה he learned, and the תורה they learned from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that her trust from Step 9 was justified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא gives his wife credit for all of his Torah and all of his students' Torah.

steps.title: כלבא שבוע has his vow released
steps.stepSummary: כלבא שבוע hears what happened, goes to have his vow undone, and it is undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: כלבא שבוע heard about it. He came and asked to be released from his vow, and it was undone, and he was released.
steps.whatsHappening: Her father hears that the great רב is his son-in-law. He goes and has his vow against them released.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said her father had cut her off through a נדר of הנאה, which is why the story belongs in מסכת נדרים. Once he hears that the great רב is his son-in-law, he goes and has the vow released, and the break between them is mended.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked to have his vow undone
it was undone, it was released

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with a נדר being released. That ties this whole story about רבי עקיבא and his wife into מסכת נדרים.

phrases.english: (Bar) Kalba Savua heard,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't; either way, it means her father, כלבא שבוע.

phrases.english: he came and asked to be released from his vow,
phrases.notes: This is the vow by which he cut his daughter off, back in Step 2.

phrases.english: and it was undone, and he was released.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by undoing the father's vow from Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלבא שבוע's vow against his daughter is released once he learns who his son-in-law has become.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא became rich from six things, starting with his father-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a list of six sources of רבי עקיבא's wealth. The first is כלבא שבוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא became rich from six things. The first is from כלבא שבוע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new list of how the once-poor רבי עקיבא became wealthy. The first item ties directly to the story just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3-4 showed a couple too poor to have anything but straw. Now the גמרא lists six sources of wealth, starting with his father-in-law, whose vow was just undone. The next steps fill in the rest of the list.

phrases.aramaic: מִן שֵׁית מִילֵּי אִיעַתַּר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: From six things Rabbi Akiva became rich:
from Kalba Savua,
phrases.notes: Now that the vow is undone, his father-in-law could give them money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן שֵׁית מִילֵּי אִיעַתַּר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new list, connected to the story through its first item, כלבא שבוע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's wealth came from six sources, the first being his father-in-law.

steps.title: Second source: a ship's ram figure left on the shore
steps.stepSummary: Ships had a carved sheep figure. Once one was forgotten on the shore, and רבי עקיבא found it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the ram of a ship. For every ship, they make a kind of sheep figure. One time they forgot it on the seashore, and he came and found it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second item on the list and briefly explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא first explains what a ship's ram is: a carved sheep figure made for every ship. Then it tells how one was left behind and רבי עקיבא found it, and that is how it made him rich.

keyTerms.meaning: the ram figure of a ship

phrases.english: from the ram of a ship.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל סְפִינָתָא עָבְדִין לֵיהּ מִין עָינָא.
phrases.english: For every ship they make a kind of sheep.
phrases.notes: A carved figure shaped like a sheep, made for the ship.

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנָא חֲדָא אַנְשְׁיוּהּ עַל כֵּיף יַמָּא
phrases.english: One time they forgot it on the seashore;
he came and found it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second item on the list of six.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא became rich from a ship's ram figure that was left on the shore.

steps.title: Third source: the sailors bring him only a log
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא paid sailors four זוז to bring him something. They found only a log on the shore and apologized for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from a log. One time he gave four זוז to sailors and said to them: Bring me something. They found nothing but a log on the seashore. They brought it to him and said: Our master, make do with this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the third item, the log. Here it sets up the story: the sailors bring what looks like a worthless piece of wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He paid for something worthwhile, and all they could find was a plain log. The sailors are apologizing, which sets up the surprise in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a log, a trunk of wood

phrases.english: And from a log,

phrases.aramaic: דְּזִימְנָא חֲדָא יְהֵיב אַרְבָּעָה זוּזֵי לְסָפוֹנָאֵי,
phrases.english: for one time he gave four zuz to sailors;
he said to them: Bring me something.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אַשְׁכַּחוּ אֶלָּא גְּווֹזָא עַל כֵּיף יַמָּא.
phrases.english: And they found nothing but a log on the seashore.
They brought it to him.
They said to him: Our master, make do with this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third item on the list of six.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third source of wealth is a log the sailors brought him.

steps.title: The log turns out to be full of coins
steps.stepSummary: The log was full of דינרים, because goods from a sunken ship had been hidden inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turned out that it was full of דינרים. For one time a ship sank, and all the goods had been put into that log, and it was found at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the surprise: the plain log was full of money. The גמרא explains how the money got inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ship had sunk, and its valuables had been stored inside this log. The log washed up and was found right when the sailors went looking for something for רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: It turned out that it was full of dinars.
For one time a ship sank,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלֵּי עִיסְקָא הֲוָה מַחֵית בְּהָהוּא גְּווֹזָא,
phrases.english: and all the goods had been put into that log,
and it was found at that time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the log story from Step 14 with its surprise ending.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worthless-looking log held a sunken ship's money, which made רבי עקיבא rich.

steps.title: Fourth and fifth sources: the סרוקיתא and a noble lady
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the next two sources on the list: the סרוקיתא and a מטרוניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from the סרוקיתא, and from a noble lady.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the fourth and fifth items on the list without telling their stories yet. This line sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the list has five of the six items. Only the names are given here. Their details, and the sixth item, continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: the Serukita, a group of traders

phrases.english: and from the Serukita,
phrases.notes: Only the name is given here; the story itself comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: and from a noble lady,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of six after the log story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth and fifth sources of רבי עקיבא's wealth are the סרוקיתא and a מטרוניתא.
